queries.question: If expected_source_count is left at zero, when does the status aggregator consider all sources reported, and does source-manifest still arm the seed timeout?
queries.answer: With expectedCount <= 0, allReported no longer waits for a count: it is true as soon as at least one report has arrived (len(reports) > 0). startSeedTimeout returns nil before arming the timer when ExpectedSourceCount <= 0, so no seed-timeout goroutine runs and the status is never marked degraded by timeout; with a positive count the timer (SeedTimeout, fallback 120s) fires markDegraded unless seedComplete is already set.
queries.rationale: allReported holds the zero-expected rule (any single report counts as all reported); startSeedTimeout holds the early return that never arms the timer when ExpectedSourceCount <= 0. Each entity answers one half and neither mentions the other's rule, so no single entity establishes both.

queries.question: Why is a stable total_entities no longer an acceptable readiness signal, and which fields does the HTTP status endpoint add so a client can gate on index and embedding readiness instead?
queries.answer: On a big one-shot ingest embeddings (even BM25) lag structural readiness, so the old "total_entities is stable" heuristic is retired: counts are no longer a readiness proxy. Poll until embedding.ready is true before trusting code_search; index.ready gates the structural tools. GET /status takes the pre-marshaled status and adds top-level index (structural index readiness), embedding (semantic index readiness) and note fields; they are additive so namespace/phase/sources are untouched, and a failed sub-query yields an explicit {available:false, reason} object rather than omitting the key.
queries.rationale: The tiers README passage explains why counts are not readiness (embedding lag; the stable-count heuristic is retired) and names embedding.ready and index.ready; handleStatus shows that GET /status is where they are surfaced, as additive top-level index/embedding/note fields with {available:false, reason} on failure. The passage never mentions the HTTP envelope and the handler never explains the lag.

queries.question: Under what exact conditions does the readiness note say a lookup miss is a genuine absence rather than not-yet-ingested, and which tools do index.ready and embedding.ready each make reliable?
queries.answer: A miss is a genuine absence only when status.phase is "ready" (every configured source has finished its initial seed) AND the relevant index signal is ready; while status.phase is "seeding" a miss may simply be not-yet-ingested. index.ready means the structural index (NAME_INDEX) has caught up to the latest committed write, so byName / code_context / code_impact are reliable; embedding.ready means the semantic pipeline has caught up, so code_search is reliable (surfaced, not gated). For exact read-your-write freshness compare the numeric indexed_revision against the write's revision.
queries.rationale: ReadinessNote is the verbatim contract string: both gates, the per-signal tool lists and the indexed_revision rule. The lookalike is the tiers README passage at configs/tiers/README.md:35-38, which says to poll embedding.ready and that index.ready gates structural tools but states no genuine-absence rule; handleStatus only embeds the note by reference.
